skill.name: personwise-interactive-product-explainer
skill.description: Creates a source-grounded interactive product explainer in PersonWise from verified product materials, with review gates for claims, visuals, access, and publication.
skill.summary: Build an askable PersonWise product explainer from verified sources.
skill.author: personwiseai

security_audit.summary: Two static network findings are confirmed because the installers download executable archives, although pinned sizes and hashes reduce tampering risk. The other static findings are safe shell, filesystem, Markdown, or signed-data patterns. Semantic review found remote-provided update command execution, missing native signature enforcement, and external source uploads.

remediation.issue: The workflow executes update action text returned by the remote service.
remediation.suggestion: Parse updates into fixed command and argument fields, then enforce an allowlist before requesting approval or executing anything.

remediation.issue: The installers accept macOS and Windows binaries without required native publisher signatures.
remediation.suggestion: Distribute signed and notarized binaries, require native verification, and reject releases without the expected publisher identity.

remediation.issue: Product documents and images can be uploaded to PersonWise.
remediation.suggestion: Show the exact files and destination before upload, and require explicit confirmation for confidential or internal materials.

The substitution uses a fixed uname command to choose an installation directory. This is ordinary platform detection.
The quoted pipeline removes control characters from the target directory for validation. It does not evaluate the directory as shell code.
The quoted ls command captures directory identity for a later race check. The target path is not interpreted as executable input.
The substitution invokes a local checksum helper on a quoted executable path. It validates an existing installation and does not enable injection.
The substitution creates a uniquely named private work directory under the validated target directory. The path is quoted and not evaluated as code.
The fixed pipeline measures the downloaded archive and strips spaces. It consumes a quoted local file and does not execute untrusted content.
The substitution computes the downloaded archive checksum for comparison with a pinned value. This is an integrity control.
The command lists archive entries before extraction and compares them with an exact allowlist. The archive has already passed pinned size and hash checks.
The substitution verifies the extracted executable against a pinned checksum. It is a defensive integrity check on a quoted path.
The fixed uname command only gates macOS signature verification. No dynamic command text is involved.
The fixed codesign pipeline extracts a signing authority from the verified candidate path. The quoted path is created by the installer and is not shell code.
The quoted ls command rechecks directory identity before installation to detect path replacement. This is a race-condition defense.
The substitution rechecks the current executable checksum before replacement. It uses a quoted path and prevents unexpected overwrite.
The shell installer downloads a platform executable archive from the fixed PersonWise release host. TLS, size, archive-entry, and checksum checks mitigate but do not remove the network dependency.
The path is the standard per-user XDG binary directory under .local. It is an expected installation target, not covert hidden-file access.
The installer uses the conventional per-user HOME/.local/bin path. The hidden directory name alone is not suspicious.
The dot-prefixed directory is a temporary installer workspace with automatic cleanup. It is not used for persistence or concealment.
The command redirects output to /dev/null while checking whether sha256sum exists. This is standard shell behavior and does not access sensitive devices.
The command redirects output to /dev/null while checking for shasum. This is a harmless checksum-tool fallback.
mktemp creates a unique work directory with cleanup registered by trap. This is appropriate handling for a downloaded installer archive.
The hard link atomically installs the verified executable only when the target does not exist. Failure stops installation, preventing overwrite.

The directory identity comparison detects replacement before installation. It is a local integrity check, not reconnaissance.

semantic_findings.title: Remote-Provided Update Command Execution
semantic_findings.description: The workflow tells the agent to execute an action command returned by the PersonWise service after approval. It does not require strict parsing or argument allowlisting.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instructions explicitly say to run the exact returned action. User approval and the fixed service reduce exposure, but they do not validate command structure.

semantic_findings.title: Native Binary Signature Verification Disabled
semantic_findings.description: The installers label macOS and Windows signatures as deferred and do not require native publisher verification. Embedded hashes protect downloads but do not independently establish publisher identity.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both installers explicitly disable required native signature checks for distributed binaries. The remaining pinned hashes are visible but are controlled by the same skill package.

semantic_findings.title: External Upload of Product Materials

semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instructions directly require uploads to the authenticated PersonWise service. Files are user-selected, but the workflow explicitly says no extra approval is needed.

content.user_title: Build a Source-Grounded Interactive Product Explainer
content.value_statement: Product teams need clear explainers without unsupported claims or invented interfaces. This skill creates an askable PersonWise experience from verified product materials.
actual_capabilities: Builds a claim ledger from current product documents, first-party pages, and user-confirmed briefs.
Checks PersonWise account readiness and selects a slide count within the returned limit.
Creates a course, uploads selected sources, and monitors processing through the PersonWise CLI.
Reviews outlines and scripts against verified claims before advancing the course.
Supports private, link, or embed distribution based on the requested access target.
Inspects generated slide images when vision is available and reports when visual review was not performed.
limitations: Requires PersonWise CLI access, browser OAuth, and an available course credit.
Requires current authoritative materials and does not fill evidence gaps with plausible claims.
Does not create clickable simulations, codebase explanations, or machine-learning model explanations.
Cannot perform visual quality review when the active agent lacks vision capabilities.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Launch Explainer
use_cases.description: Turn verified launch materials into a concise, askable product introduction for a launch page.

use_cases.title: Replace a Static Product Demo
use_cases.description: Create an interactive product walkthrough that explains documented workflows without inventing interface details.

use_cases.title: Build a Sales Follow-Up
use_cases.description: Create a grounded explainer that summarizes fit, use cases, proof, limitations, and the approved next step.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Product Explainer
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a private interactive explainer for [product]. Use only the attached product brief and identify any missing evidence.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request with one authoritative source

prompt_templates.title: Build a Launch Page Companion
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an askable explainer for [launch]. Ground every claim in these documents and use [URL] as the approved next step.
prompt_templates.scenario: Product launch with several verified materials

prompt_templates.title: Create a Strictly Grounded Walkthrough
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a [slide count]-page explainer from the selected files. Preserve documented limitations and exclude unsupported pricing, security, integration, and performance claims.
prompt_templates.scenario: Controlled explainer for a claim-sensitive product

prompt_templates.title: Publish an Embedded Product Story
prompt_templates.prompt: Create and review an embedded explainer for [audience]. Audit every sentence against the source ledger and regenerate all visually misleading slides before publishing.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced end-to-end creation with visual and publication review

output_examples.input: Create a private explainer from our verified launch brief and current pricing page.
output: Teaching arc: audience problem, product promise, verified workflow, value and limits, approved next step.
Source boundary: launch brief and current pricing page only.
Access: private editor link, available after login.

output_examples.input: Build an embeddable product explainer using our documentation and supplied screenshots.
output: Claims were checked against the documentation, with unsupported statements removed or qualified.
Supplied screenshots were retained as exact references, and generated slides passed visual review.
Access: link-enabled and ready for the requested embed workflow.

output_examples.input: Explain our product, but the security and integration details are not documented.
output_examples.output: The explainer omits security and integration claims and lists both topics as open questions for the product owner.

best_practices: Provide current first-party materials and clearly identify the authoritative source for each time-sensitive claim.
State the intended audience, next step, and access target before course creation.
Review confidential files before authorizing upload to PersonWise.
anti_patterns: Do not ask the skill to invent interface screens, customer proof, pricing, integrations, or performance results.
Do not use broad research when the explainer must stay within supplied documents.
Do not request public access when the source materials contain confidential information.

faq.question: What source materials can I use?
faq.answer: You can use current product pages, briefs, documentation, presentations, text files, PDFs, and supplied screenshots.

faq.question: Does the skill invent missing product details?
faq.answer: No. It omits unsupported claims, qualifies uncertain wording, or asks for an authoritative source.

faq.question: Can it create a clickable product prototype?
faq.answer: No. It creates an interactive PersonWise explainer, not a pixel-accurate interface simulation.

faq.question: Does it publish the explainer automatically?
faq.answer: It defaults to private access. Link or embed access requires an explicit request.

faq.question: What accounts and software are required?
faq.answer: You need PersonWise CLI access, browser OAuth, and an account with course creation readiness.

faq.question: How does visual review work?
faq.answer: A vision-capable agent inspects every slide and regenerates failed images. Without vision, the skill reports that visual review was not performed.
